author: ValWood
body:
I'm sorry. I just edited the title. I wasn't correcting you, @ccasalsc. I thought I was correcting myself! because I was looking at this in the past couple of days.

I have been trying to figure out the relationships.

Pombe has 
min8 / SPAPB8E5.10.  mapped to  COXFA4, COXFA4L2, COXFA4L3
mra2/ SPBC3H7.08c. mapped to  COXFA4, COXFA4L2, COXFA4L3
SPCC417.16  mapped to  COXFA4, COXFA4L2, COXFA4L3


COXFA4, COXFA4L2, COXFA4L3 are the new names for  NDUFA4, NDUFA4L2 and C15orf48 respectively
(these are probably not appropriate names if these proteins are specific for different respiratory chain assembly steps)

There is also COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2), which I have not currently mapped to pombe.

I noticed recently that these appear to likely be independent orthologs and seem to have different specificities for respiratory complex assembly.

So far, we know that in yeast 
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38508182/
mra1 (min8 or mra2 in pombe) https://www.cell.com/cms/10.1016/j.devcel.2024.02.011/asset/cdd78bd2-c7ed-48b4-b90d-797bbf7d9d9d/main.assets/gr2_lrg.jpg
is cytochrome oxidase assembly (and then gets degraded as part of the stop-GO signal for ATPase assembly)

In humans, COXFA4 is cytochrome oxidase (complex IV-associated).


I wonder if PANTHER could rebuild and extend the family to include all of the orthologs so that we can see clearly how they are related to each other  I assume they are all required in different steps of respiratory complex assembly.


pombe mra2 is only in 
https://pantherdb.org/panther/family.do?clsAccession=PTHR40466

pombe SPCC417.16 and min8 are in 
https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/pfam/PF06522/
**NADH-ubiquinone reductase complex 1 MLRQ subunit**
(but pombe and cerevisiae do not have complex I)
which includes 
PTHR14256 NADH-UBIQUINONE OXIDOREDUCTASE MLRQ SUBUNIT
BUT  SPCC417.16 and min8  do not appear to be in the pPanther family.

This is as far as a got .....I was going to try Jackhmmer next, and try to get PFAM updated but it would be better if  it was sorted by PANTHER from a GO curation perspective.

author: ccasalsc
body:
No worries,
I haven't gone so far... it just than in the literature they say it's part of complex I since it was thought that COXFA4 was part of complex I, now we know it is a component of complex IV.
However there is no evidence that it is a component of complex I, since when it is deleted, the complex I composition doesn't change, but it inhibits it's activity (PubMed=22100406). So for now it is specific molecular function and subcellular location are not really known.
About COXFA4L3, it has been prove that it can replace COXFA4 as component of complex IV upon inflammatory stimuli.
That's all I have.

Cristina

body: On my side, I've restricted the annotation of the term complex IV. I let  the ticket open at least until we have feedback from @huaiyumi about the tree rebuilding.

author: marcfeuermann
body: It has been added to the list of families for which the topology must be modified. As I've corrected the PAINT annotation, I close this ticket. All the families will be rePAINTed once the topology will be updated.
